name: Tallinn University of Technology
summary: Technical university in Tallinn (founded 1918) with four English-taught bachelor's; the two engineering degrees are tuition-free for EU/EEA citizens.

handoff.label: Bachelor's and master's programmes taught in English

ib.text: Upload the IB Diploma (marked 'Diploma awarded'; course results do not count) and a transcript. IB or European Baccalaureate graduates need no English test. Each degree adds an online test or letter and an interview.

programmes.name: Integrated Engineering
programmes.about: Combines ICT with mechanical and electrical engineering; you study programming, computer-aided design, robotics and digital manufacturing, with a semester abroad possible through Erasmus+.
programmes.selectionNote: Proctored online test (maths, physics, chemistry, IT; 60 of 100 to pass), then an online interview; 60 combined admits you. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Cyber Security Engineering
programmes.about: Design, build and maintain secure IT systems, mixing hands-on work with theory; deep prior maths, programming or IT knowledge is helpful but not essential.
programmes.selectionNote: Online test (60 of 100 to pass), then interview and motivation letter scored together (60 needed). 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: International Business Administration
programmes.about: Builds knowledge and skills for an international business career, taught in English at the School of Business and Governance, with specialisations chosen within the degree.
programmes.ib: Motivation letter and CV are scored, with an online maths test and an interview; EU citizens pay the same fee as non-EU.
programmes.selectionNote: Average of 60 points across motivation letter, CV and online maths test, plus 5 points at the online interview, admits you. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Law
programmes.about: Classical legal principles alongside technology law, cyber security and data protection law, EU and international law, with moot court and a legal internship.
programmes.ib: An online test comes first, then an interview assessing English, expression and argument; EU citizens pay the same fee as non-EU.
programmes.selectionNote: Online test, then an interview scored with your motivation letter and CV; 50 points in total admits you. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: Study is tuition-free for EU/EEA citizens except in the School of Business and Governance, which covers International Business Administration and Law.
Finnish, Latvian and Lithuanian citizens applying to the School of Business and Governance have their own, later deadline.
Estonian citizens and long-term residents apply through the national SAIS system; international applicants use DreamApply.
